newsitem.title: USA: Union Pacific suit seeks Pennzoil merger approval.
newsitem.headline: Union Pacific suit seeks Pennzoil merger approval.

text.p: Union Pacific Resources Group Inc said, in a lawsuit filed on Monday, that it wants the Delaware Chancery Court to compel Pennzoil Company directors to approve a proposed $6.4 billion merger and to refrain from using any anti-takeover defenses against the tender offer.

In court papers made available to Reuters on Tuesday, Union Pacific alleged a court order was necessary because Pennzoil directors "have signaled in no uncertain terms that they will seek to defeat the tender offer and merger."

According to the lawsuit, Pennzoil proposed a merger with Union Pacific in 1995 that Pennzoil allegedly said would create the "premier exploration and production company in the world." But now the Pennzoil directors have "rebuffed Union Pacific...(and say) Pennzoil should remain an independent, publicly-held company," court papers say.
Union Pacific alleges Pennzoil's directors will use anti- takeover defenses to "unlawfully entrench themselves in office...to the irreparable detriment of plaintiffs and the Pennzoil stockholders."

The defenses include a rights plan or poison pill which would make a takeover "economically unfeasible" by allowing Pennnzoil shareholders to buy $280 worth of Pennzoil common stock for $140 when an investor acquires at least 15 percent of the shares.

Pennzoil could also invoke either the Delaware Business Combination law that puts any takeover on hold for three years unless it is first approved by the directors; or its own charter requirement that 80 percent of the common stock must be voted in favor of any merger.
Pennzoil spokesman Robert Harper told Reuters "The lawsuit is not unexpected. The rhetoric is not unexpected and Pennzoil will be filing its response in due course."
